name: Badge
description: A small status indicator component for displaying tags, counts, or status information
designIntent: The Badge component is used to display small pieces of information like status indicators, counts, or tags. It provides visual variants for different semantic meanings (default, secondary, destructive, outline).

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic surface; primary/danger are aliases for default/destructive, neutral is a muted metadata pill and accent is a tinted brand pill.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to display inside the badge

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the child element with badge styling.

examples.title: Default badge
examples.description: Primary badge for highlighting new items

examples.title: Secondary badge
examples.description: Less prominent badge for secondary information

examples.title: Destructive badge
examples.description: Badge for error states or destructive actions

examples.title: Count badge
examples.description: Badge for displaying counts or numbers

antiPatterns.title: Don't use for long text
antiPatterns.explanation: Badges are designed for short text. Use tooltips or other components for longer content.

antiPatterns.title: Don't overuse badges
antiPatterns.explanation: Too many badges create visual noise. Prioritize the most important information.
antiPatterns.example:
// Avoid: Too many badges
New Updated Featured Popular
// Prefer: Consolidate or prioritize
New Featured

antiPatterns.title: Don't use wrong variant for meaning
antiPatterns.explanation: Destructive variant should only be used for errors or destructive actions.

accessibility.implementation: Badge content is announced as text. Use aria-label if badge has visual-only meaning
accessibility.userRequirements: For status badges, consider adding aria-label to convey meaning

accessibility.implementation: All variants meet WCAG AA contrast requirements
accessibility.userRequirements: Test custom colors for contrast in both light and dark modes

accessibility.implementation: Badge has visible focus ring when keyboard navigable
accessibility.userRequirements: If badge is interactive, ensure it can be keyboard navigated

guidelines: Keep badge text very short (1-2 words ideally)
Use sentence case for badge text
Use standard status terms (Active, Inactive, Pending, etc.)
Be consistent with status terminology across the application
Consider color coding to reinforce status meaning

compositionRules.relationship: Badges can be combined with buttons to show notification counts or status
Badges are often used in card headers to show status or category
